incidente.resumo: Threat actors used an authentication token compromised at Okta, apparently hijacked from a Cloudflare support ticket in Okta's customer support system, to access Cloudflare's Okta instance with administrative privileges and compromised two Cloudflare employee accounts in the Okta platform. Cloudflare detected the activity internally and its security team contained the incident using its Zero Trust tools before the attackers reached customer data, customer systems or the production network; no customer information or systems were impacted.

descricao.texto: Cloudflare detected the attack activity internally, through its Security Incident Response Team's real-time detection, more than 24 hours before Okta notified it of the breach.
trechos: While this was a troubling security incident, our Security Incident Response Team’s (SIRT) real-time detection and prompt response enabled containment and minimized the impact to Cloudflare systems and data.
We detected this activity internally more than 24 hours before we were notified of the breach by Okta.

descricao.texto: Threat actors leveraged an authentication token compromised at Okta to pivot into Cloudflare's Okta instance, using an open session with administrative privileges; Okta's customer support system had been accessed, and it appears the token was hijacked from a support ticket created by a Cloudflare employee. Two Cloudflare employee accounts within the Okta platform were compromised.
trechos: On Wednesday, October 18, 2023, we discovered attacks on our system that we were able to trace back to Okta – threat actors were able to leverage an authentication token compromised at Okta to pivot into Cloudflare’s Okta instance.
The attacker used an open session from Okta, with Administrative privileges, and accessed our Okta instance.
According to Okta’s statement, the threat-actor accessed Okta’s customer support system and viewed files uploaded by certain Okta customers as part of recent support cases.
It appears that in our case, the threat-actor was able to hijack a session token from a support ticket which was created by a Cloudflare employee.
In this sophisticated attack, we observed that threat-actors compromised two separate Cloudflare employee accounts within the Okta platform.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: According to Cloudflare, Okta was first notified of a compromise on October 2, 2023 by BeyondTrust, but the attacker still had access to Okta's support systems at least until October 18, 2023.
trechos: Take any report of compromise seriously and act immediately to limit damage; in this case Okta was first notified on October 2, 2023 by BeyondTrust but the attacker still had access to their support systems at least until October 18, 2023.

passos.texto: Using Cloudflare Zero Trust Access, Gateway, Data Loss Prevention and Cloudforce One threat research, the security team contained the incident before the attacker could gain access to customer data, customer systems or the production network, and mitigated it before the threat actors could establish persistence.
trechos: We were able to use our Cloudflare Zero Trust Access, Gateway, and Data Loss Prevention and our Cloudforce One threat research to validate the scope of the incident and contain it before the attacker could gain access to customer data, customer systems, or our production network.
With this confidence, we were able to quickly mitigate the incident before the threat-actors were able to establish persistence.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta: take any report of compromise seriously and act immediately to limit damage.
trechos: Take any report of compromise seriously and act immediately to limit damage; in this case Okta was first notified on October 2, 2023 by BeyondTrust but the attacker still had access to their support systems at least until October 18, 2023.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta: provide timely, responsible disclosures to customers affected by a breach.
trechos: Provide timely, responsible disclosures to your customers when you identify that a breach of your systems has affected them.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta: require hardware keys to protect all systems, including third-party support providers.
trechos: Require hardware keys to protect all systems, including third-party support providers.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta's customers: enable hardware MFA for all user accounts, preferring hardware keys over other MFA methods.
trechos: Enable Hardware MFA for all user accounts.
We strongly recommend the usage of hardware keys, as other methods of MFA can be vulnerable to phishing attacks.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta's customers: monitor for new or reactivated Okta users, Okta account and permission changes, MFA policy overrides, changes and removal, and supply chain providers accessing their tenants.
trechos: New Okta users created.
Reactivation of Okta users.
All Okta account and permission changes.
MFA policy overrides, MFA changes, and MFA removal.
Supply chain providers accessing your tenants.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to Okta's customers: review session expiration policies to limit session hijack attacks, and use tools to validate devices connected to critical systems, such as Cloudflare Access Device Posture Check.
trechos: Review session expiration policies to limit session hijack attacks.
Utilize tools to validate devices connected to your critical systems, such as Cloudflare Access Device Posture Check.

observacoes: All prevention items are recommendations Cloudflare gives to Okta and to Okta's customers, not Cloudflare commitments. Cloudflare says no customer information or systems were impacted. The text mentions an earlier Okta breach in March 2022 that did not reach Cloudflare systems; it is not part of this record. deteccao.forma is nao_informada: the text says the activity was detected internally through SIRT 'real-time detection' but not whether an alert fired or staff noticed it.
